_note: URL changes made while the site was being built. None of these old paths was ever indexed — the site has carried noindex throughout — so no link equity is at stake. They are recorded anyway because someone may have bookmarked a preview URL, and because a redirect map is far easier to keep than to reconstruct later.
_hosting: Emitted twice from this one source. /.htaccess is read by Apache and LiteSpeed, which is what serves the site today, so that is the file doing the work. /_redirects is the Netlify and Cloudflare Pages format, kept so a move between hosts does not silently drop the map. Neither host reads the other's file, so both being present is harmless. GitHub Pages reads neither; a project site there cannot serve 301s at all.
_order: First match wins, so a wildcard must come after every specific rule that shares its prefix — otherwise the wildcard swallows them and the renamed slugs never reach their new URLs. Keep specifics above their splat.
